# `liber:import@1`

Generated reference for the `liber:import` package (`import.lsidl`). See [the LSIDL language](../../../LSIDL.md).

LiberSystem media import - objects read from a camera's Picture Transfer Protocol storage, for a component PermissionManager granted `media-import`.  A CAMERA IS AN OBJECT SOURCE, NOT A VOLUME. A client lists devices and their storages, takes a bounded snapshot of one storage's object handles and pages through it for typed metadata, and reads one object at a time in bounded chunks. It cannot send a command, reach a catalogue or a backend, write anywhere, delete or capture: the service is a source and nothing else, and it holds no storage of its own to write into.  EVERY IDENTITY IS SCOPED AND EXPIRES. A device, storage or object identity carries the publication, the attachment epoch, the PTP session, the content epoch and the service incarnation. A change the device reports, a dropped event, a reset, a lost session or a withdrawal advances one of them, and everything named under the old one is stale - a numeric object handle alone is never enough to reach an object again.  COMPLETION IS NEVER INFERRED. A transfer ends `complete` only after every expected byte and the device's matching successful final response; anything else is `partial`, with the count delivered and the cause. A short or empty chunk is not an end, and a lost connection without a final status is an unknown outcome.  WHAT A CONSUMER OWES ITS DESTINATION. Publish a normal, completed destination only after a `complete` ending. A storage consumer writes through `volume.open-writer`, commits only on `complete`, and aborts on `partial`, on an error and on a lost connection - within that writer's own size cap. An import larger than that cap needs a staging consumer specified for it; nothing here promises one.

## Interfaces

### interface `media-import`

DEVICES, STORAGES, AND THE TWO CAPABILITIES A CLIENT CAN BE GIVEN: a cursor over a snapshot, and one object's transfer. One of each at a time per client and per device.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `limits` | `limits() -> result<import-limits, error>` |  |
| 2 | `devices` | `devices() -> result<list<import-device>, error>` |  |
| 3 | `storages` | `storages(device: import-device-id) -> result<list<import-storage>, error>` |  |
| 4 | `open-enumeration` | `open-enumeration(storage: import-storage-id, parent: option<import-parent-id>) -> result<import-enumeration, error>` |  |
| 5 | `open-read` | `open-read(object: import-object-id) -> result<handle<channel>, error>` |  |

### interface `import-cursor`

A SNAPSHOT OF HANDLES, and metadata fetched for them as they are paged - current when fetched.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `next` | `next() -> result<import-page, error>` |  |
| 2 | `close` | `close() -> result<unit, error>` |  |

### interface `import-transfer`

ONE OBJECT, IN ORDER. `read` answers a chunk at its exact offset or the terminal status.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `read` | `read() -> result<import-read, error>` |  |
| 2 | `status` | `status() -> result<import-transfer-status, error>` |  |
| 3 | `cancel` | `cancel() -> result<import-transfer-status, error>` |  |
